[00:00:00] Jenna Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, we're the Redwood team, I'm Jenna, account executive. Marco is our SE, Leah is on CSM.
[00:00:22] Priya Sen: Hi, Priya here, CISO at Veritas. We're mainly trying to validate the controls mapping before our audit next quarter.
[00:00:30] Marco Ruiz: Great. Today's goal is to show where the SOC two artifacts live in TrustCenter, how we map those to your control matrix, and then talk KMS and log exports.
[00:00:52] Marisol Vega: When you say TrustCenter, is that the web portal or you guys call it TrustCenter? I sometimes see "Trust Center" in docs.
[00:00:58] Jenna Park: Yeah both, official name is TrustCenter, our docs use both. We'll send the invite link after this.
[00:01:20] Ethan Cole: Quick ask: we need logs in a format our SIEM ingests, ideally JSON with timestamp and trace ids. Retention policy is a hard requirement.
[00:01:33] Marco Ruiz: Understood. We can export audit logs as JSON and push to your S3 or syslog collector; retention is configurable per workspace. There is a retention cap on hosted accounts but for Dedicated/Private you control retention.
[00:01:55] Samir Patel: Clarify that — Dedicated gives us more control but we might need Private for residency.
[00:02:05] Jenna Park: Right, Dedicated is reserved capacity in our cloud and you still use our TrustCenter control plane. Private gives you control plane inside your VPC or on-prem.
[00:02:26] Ava Li: For compliance, our auditors want to see SOC 2 Type II evidence and also an ISO 27001 A.18 mapping. Do you have the ISO artifacts?
[00:02:37] Leah Kim: Yes we maintain an ISO checklist; we can share the mapping doc. It's in the same TrustCenter area under "Assurance -> Controls".
[00:03:05] Priya Sen: Also KMS: we need to confirm where keys live. We use AWS KMS in eu-west-1 and require HSM-backed keys for certain data classes.
[00:03:18] Marco Ruiz: Our Private/KMS integration supports AWS KMS and external HSMs via KMS proxies. For hosted, we use a service-managed key but we also provide bring-your-own-key options for Dedicated via KMS integration.
[00:03:43] Ethan Cole: Is there a key rotation cadence exposed in the TrustCenter audit?
[00:03:50] Marco Ruiz: We log key usage and rotation events in audit logs. Rotation itself depends on your KMS policy but we capture events.
[00:04:12] Marisol Vega: On evidence exports: auditors want chain-of-custody for how log files were generated. Are exported manifests signed?
[00:04:25] Omar Shah: We produce export manifests with hashes and timestamps. They're not currently signed with an external certificate by default but we can ship signed manifests as an add-on.
[00:04:47] Jenna Park: I'll flag that as an action item, Marco to show a sample export in the next call.
[00:05:02] Priya Sen: Perfect. Also can you show us the RBAC model — mapping Redwood roles to our internal roles?
[00:05:10] Marco Ruiz: Sure. High-level: admin, auditor, operator, viewer. We can map SAML attributes to those roles. For example, group "Auditors" in your IdP gets auditor role in TrustCenter.
[00:05:37] Ethan Cole: Can we restrict access to logs to a read-only auditor role that can't spin up models?
[00:05:44] Marco Ruiz: Yes, auditor role is read-only for logs and evidence, cannot execute model endpoints.
[00:06:08] Priya Sen: Good, that helps. About the SOC 2 report: is the Type II full bundle available? We need test dates.
[00:06:18] Leah Kim: We have the latest Type II bundle with date range in the artifact. Jenna will share the PDF after the call.
[00:06:34] Priya Sen: One more thing — do you provide a CSV export of controls mapping to map to our internal GRC?
[00:06:42] Marco Ruiz: Yep, CSV/Excel exports of the mapping, with control ids and linked evidence pointers.
[00:06:59] Samir Patel: For residency, our legal requires data at rest for PII to be in eu-west-1. Would a Private deployment be necessary or can Dedicated in eu-west satisfy?
[00:07:12] Jenna Park: Dedicated can be deployed in region and isolated, but for absolute control of networking and keying Private is recommended. It depends on your policy.
[00:07:34] Ava Li: If we go Private, how does logging ingestion to our SIEM work? Any extra agents?
[00:07:42] Marco Ruiz: We can push logs to a customer S3 in the region or stream via secure syslog over TLS. You can also run our lightweight exporter inside your VPC.
[00:08:05] Ethan Cole: About encryption-at-rest — is there a default encryption algorithm you use and is that documented in the report?
[00:08:13] Omar Shah: AES-256 is used for at-rest for managed keys; for BYOK you control algorithm via your KMS provider. We document this in the trust doc.
[00:08:38] [00:08:38] Priya Sen: Ok. Let's dig into the controls map. Jenna, can you pull up the mapping sheet?
[00:08:45] Jenna Park: I'll paste a link in the chat — https://redwood.app/trustcenter/veritas-controls (note: placeholder). The mapping shows Redwood control ids, corresponding SOC 2 criteria, linked evidence samples.
[00:09:04] Marisol Vega: I see control RD-AC-02 mapped to SOC 2 CC6. We need the procedure doc for that — where is it?
[00:09:15] Marco Ruiz: The procedure doc is under Evidence -> Procedures. We'll attach a sample runbook.
[00:09:33] [00:09:33] Ethan Cole: There's some fuzziness on retention policy: logged events for admin activity need to be kept for 7 years for us. Is that supported?
[00:09:46] Marco Ruiz: For hosted that's not typical, but Dedicated + Private can be configured with your retention. For extremely long retention, we'd propose pushing exports to your S3 bucket for archiving.
[00:10:08] Priya Sen: That works, but our auditors want to see live access to the TrustCenter as well. Can auditors be onboarded as external users?
[00:10:17] Leah Kim: Yes, TrustCenter supports external auditor accounts with limited roles. We'll set up an "Auditor" role with MFA and JIT access.
[00:10:36] Samir Patel: MFA is mandatory for auditor role? We prefer MFA enforced.
[00:10:42] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we enforce MFA on auditor and admin roles and support SAML assertions for step-up auth.
[00:11:05] Priya Sen: About evidence timestamps — auditors want monotonic timestamps linked to request traces so they can verify events in sequence.
[00:11:15] Marco Ruiz: Our request tracing includes a trace id that appears in both request logs and model logs; the export manifest includes those ids. Sequencing is preserved in the logs.
[00:11:33] Marisol Vega: Can you include schema sample so our SIEM team can test ingestion?
[00:11:41] Marco Ruiz: We'll attach a sample JSON schema. Action item.
[00:11:58] Jenna Park: Quick note, competitor called ModelServeCorp surfaced in an RFP; they had a different approach to evidence signing. If you need signature-backed manifests, we can discuss as an add-on.
[00:12:12] Priya Sen: What's the timeline for a Private POC if we decide?
[00:12:20] Omar Shah: From contract to spin up it's typically 4-6 weeks, depends on network approvals. We can accelerate with a trial image for your infra team to run.
[00:12:35] [00:12:35] Ethan Cole: Network approvals tend to be the blocker, we'll start that in parallel.
[00:12:45] Jenna Park: Good. Any other compliance questions?
[00:12:50] Ava Li: Evidence access logging — can we see who downloaded what and when?
[00:12:57] Marco Ruiz: Yes, TrustCenter records artifact downloads with user id, IP, timestamp. That is part of audit logs.
[00:13:20] Priya Sen: For ISO 27001, we need to map Annex A controls to cloud provider responsibilities. Do you have a shared responsibility matrix?
[00:13:29] Leah Kim: Yes, we have an SRM that maps our controls to customer responsibilities. We'll share the matrix.
[00:13:45] Marisol Vega: Also need a statement of confidentiality for access to production models during the audit.
[00:13:52] Jenna Park: We can provide an auditor NDA template; auditors can be given read-only access.
[00:14:06] Samir Patel: Let's talk about the format for the SOC 2 breakdown — is it by control or by artifact?
[00:14:14] Marco Ruiz: Both. The TrustCenter UI shows controls with linked artifacts; the export flattens to control->artifact rows.
[00:14:37] [00:14:37] Priya Sen: Okay, I'm scanning for gaps — our next audit window is mid-Jan. We need to finalize scoping in October.
[00:14:48] Jenna Park: Action: Jenna to share SOC2 bundle, Marco to demo export, Priya to confirm KMS region.
[00:15:02] Marisol Vega: For audit sampling, will you let us pull the raw request traces for a sample window?
[00:15:10] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we can provide a sampling job that produces a zipped set for auditors with manifests.
[00:15:30] Ethan Cole: Any rate limits on export jobs? We have high volume logs.
[00:15:38] Marco Ruiz: There are throttles at platform level but for Dedicated/Private we can tune batch sizes. We'll talk more in the bench session.
[00:15:59] Priya Sen: How do you manage secret rotation for service accounts used in export jobs?
[00:16:07] Omar Shah: We recommend short-lived tokens. For Private we support your Vault or AWS STS roles for temporary credentials.
[00:16:20] Ava Li: Do you maintain an evidence retention policy in the TrustCenter?
[00:16:27] Leah Kim: Yes, default retention 90 days for hosted artifacts, configurable for Dedicated/Private. We document exceptions.
[00:16:42] Marisol Vega: Are there known gaps for ISO A.8 (asset management) in your standard profile?
[00:16:49] Marco Ruiz: In our baseline there are some inventory responsibilities shared with the customer; we'll point them out in the SRM.
[00:17:05] Priya Sen: Ok I think we have the main items. Anything else on RBAC or SSO that would prevent audit signoff?
[00:17:12] Marco Ruiz: The main ask is to ensure SAML attribute mapping is provisioned and MFA enforced.
[00:17:23] Jenna Park: Next steps recap: I'll send the SOC2 bundle and invite, Marco will schedule the export demo and provide sample schemas, and Priya will confirm KMS region.
[00:17:40] Priya Sen: Sounds good. One small question — do you support customer-managed encryption keys for logs in transit?
[00:17:48] Omar Shah: For in-transit we use TLS; customer-managed certs can be used for Private endpoints. For stored logs, BYOK is supported.
[00:18:06] Ethan Cole: Can the export manifest include a pointer to KMS key id used to encrypt a blob?
[00:18:14] Marco Ruiz: Yes we can include kms_key_id in the manifest.
[00:18:30] Marisol Vega: Great, that will help our auditors trace key usage.

[00:18:44] Priya Sen: Thanks much.
